help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The competition outstripped us long ago.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Nobody knows what he is up to.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: jemandem den Rang ablaufen takes the person in the dative: allen Konkurrenten.
help.tips[0].en.text: An idiom keeps its nouns, articles and old case endings exactly; you conjugate only the verb and add the person in the right case. mit dem Bade (never: mit dem Badewasser), im Schilde führen (never: im Schild), auf verlorenem Posten stehen (no article), jemandem (Dat) den Rang ablaufen, jemandem (Dat) reinen Wein einschenken.
help.tips[0].en.title: The form is frozen — only the verb moves
help.tips[0].en.trap: jemanden den Rang ablaufen is wrong: the person is dative — jemandem.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Anyone who throws in the towel now is throwing away a good starting position.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: auf die lange Bank schieben is neutral to formal; the other two are colloquial and used only for colour.
help.tips[1].en.text: Neutral to formal, fine in essays and commentaries: jemandem den Rang ablaufen, etwas auf die lange Bank schieben, ins Hintertreffen geraten, auf verlorenem Posten stehen, das Kind mit dem Bade ausschütten, sich etwas nicht nehmen lassen, einen Bärendienst erweisen. More colloquial, used in the press for colour: die Flinte ins Korn werfen, etwas aus dem Ärmel schütteln, Oberwasser bekommen. In an academic paper even the neutral ones are used sparingly.
help.tips[1].en.title: Register: which idioms a leading article can carry
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: With the blanket ban the legislator is throwing the baby out with the bathwater.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: With his praise he did his colleague a disservice.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: einen Bärendienst erweisen means help that backfires: the writer judges her defence as damaging.
help.tips[2].en.text: Idioms in commentary carry judgement. das Kind mit dem Bade ausschütten criticises an overreaction; auf die lange Bank schieben accuses someone of stalling; einen Bärendienst erweisen says that help backfired; auf verlorenem Posten stehen can express sympathy or mockery. In a reading task, ask what the writer thinks of the people the idiom describes.
help.tips[2].en.title: Read the stance, not just the meaning
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: In terms of experience, nobody in this team can match her.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: The administration has fallen behind in digitalisation.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: The picture is the servant handing over water to wash one’s hands: jemandem das Wasser reichen.
help.tips[3].visual.items[1].en: to take credit for others' work
help.tips[3].en.text: Most idioms are frozen images: the long bench on which court files once waited (lange Bank), the rear rank of a battle line (Hintertreffen), the servant handing a nobleman the water to wash his hands (das Wasser reichen), the knight’s coat of arms on his shield (im Schilde führen). Recall the picture and the key word follows.
help.tips[3].en.title: Remember the picture
help.vocab[1].en: to put sth off, shelve sth
help.vocab[4].en: to tell sb the plain truth
help.vocab[5].en: to throw the baby out with the bathwater
help.vocab[10].en: to be a match for sb
help.context.en: For years the government shelved the railway reform. Meanwhile the country has fallen behind in rail transport, and its neighbours outstripped it long ago. But anyone who now wants to privatise the entire railway is throwing the baby out with the bathwater. A viable plan cannot be conjured out of thin air — but throwing in the towel would be the worst of all solutions. It is time to tell citizens the plain truth.
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: The idiom keeps the old dative form Bade; the English bathwater does not carry over.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: The idiom has no article, so the adjective takes the strong ending -em.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: The person who is overtaken is in the dative; den Rang is the accusative object.
help.mistakes[3].whyEn: im Schilde is frozen with the old dative -e.
help.hookEn: Read German commentary like a native: the idioms of the quality press, their frozen forms, and the judgement hidden in each.
help.introEn: Idioms (Redewendungen) are not proverbs: a proverb is a complete sentence with a moral (Aller Anfang ist schwer), an idiom is a fixed phrase that you build into your own sentence and conjugate — jemandem den Rang ablaufen, etwas auf die lange Bank schieben, ins Hintertreffen geraten. Commentaries, leading articles and essays are full of them, and a fluent reader has to understand the figurative meaning at once and recognise the writer’s stance behind it. This quiz drills sixteen idioms of educated press German. Each gap is the decisive word or pair of words — the part that cannot be swapped for a synonym (Bade, not Wasser; Schilde, not Plan) — the English cue gives the meaning, and the German line above the sentence paraphrases it. Learn each idiom with its fixed form: old dative -e (mit dem Bade, im Schilde), article-less strong endings (auf verlorenem Posten), the dative person (jemandem das Wasser reichen) and the verb it belongs to.
help.rememberEn[0]: An idiom is a fixed phrase inside your own sentence; a proverb is a complete sentence with a moral.
help.rememberEn[1]: Keep the frozen form: mit dem Bade, im Schilde, auf verlorenem Posten; conjugate only the verb.
help.rememberEn[2]: The person is dative: jemandem den Rang ablaufen, jemandem das Wasser reichen, jemandem reinen Wein einschenken.
help.rememberEn[3]: In commentary an idiom is a judgement — read what the writer thinks of the people it describes.
sentences[0].whyEn: jemandem den Rang ablaufen — to outstrip someone.
sentences[1].whyEn: auf die lange Bank schieben — to shelve indefinitely.
sentences[2].whyEn: ins Hintertreffen geraten — to fall behind.
sentences[3].whyEn: auf keinen grünen Zweig kommen — never to prosper.
sentences[4].whyEn: reinen Wein einschenken — to tell the unvarnished truth.
sentences[5].whyEn: das Kind mit dem Bade ausschütten — the baby with the bathwater.
sentences[6].whyEn: es sich nicht nehmen lassen — to insist on doing it oneself.
sentences[7].whyEn: aus dem Ärmel schütteln — to conjure from one's sleeve.
sentences[8].whyEn: die Flinte ins Korn werfen — to give up.
sentences[9].whyEn: auf verlorenem Posten stehen — fighting a losing battle.
sentences[10].whyEn: jemandem das Wasser reichen können — to be someone's equal.
sentences[11].whyEn: den Faden verlieren — to lose the thread.
sentences[12].whyEn: etwas im Schilde führen — to be secretly up to something.
sentences[13].whyEn: Oberwasser bekommen — to gain the upper hand.
sentences[14].whyEn: einen Bärendienst erweisen — the bear's disservice: well meant, badly done.
sentences[15].whyEn: den Stein ins Rollen bringen — to set the stone rolling.
